### Observed differences

- The elapsed time between the completion of A34 and the completion of A14 roughly doubled. In the earlier window it centred on about 1 hour (median about 1.0 h, middle half between about 0.9 and 1.1 h); in the later window it centred on about 2 hours (median about 2.0 h, middle half between about 1.8 and 2.1 h) — an increase of about 1 hour. [TWAIT001]
- The shift covers the whole distribution rather than a few outliers: mean, median and both quartiles rose by roughly 0.9–1.0 hours, and the spread widened (standard deviation from about 0.17 h to about 0.32 h). [TWAIT001]
- The pairing itself was observed at similar rates: about 98 of 200 traces in the earlier window and about 93 of 200 in the later window, roughly half of the traces in both. [TWAIT001]
- Screening produced no qualifying control-flow items (0 of 52 units, against about 0.26 expected by chance); the timing item above was the only qualifying item overall (1 of 18 time units, against about 0.009 expected by chance). [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in timing between A34 and A14: in the later window, the elapsed time from the completion of A34 to the completion of A14 is about twice as long as before (median about 2.0 hours versus about 1.0 hour), with the entire distribution shifted upward rather than only a few extreme cases. Supporting signs: the increase is consistent across the mean, median and both quartiles (each up by roughly 0.9–1.0 hours); it rests on substantial observation counts (98 versus 93 observed intervals, roughly half of the 200 traces per window); a difference this large appeared in only about 1 of 2,000 random re-splits of the pooled data; and the time family's chance expectation was about 0.009 items, so one qualifying time item is roughly a hundredfold that expectation, while control flow produced 0 items against about 0.26 expected — consistent with a pure timing change without structural rearrangement at these thresholds. Limitations: T_WAIT measures elapsed time between consecutive completion events, so the evidence cannot show whether the extra hour reflects longer waiting, handover or processing, nor what happens between the two completions; and the absence of control-flow items rules out structural change only at the configured thresholds, not entirely. [TWAIT001]

Other differences: The number of observed A34–A14 intervals dipped slightly, from 98 to 93 (about 5 fewer in 100); no control-flow indicator qualified, so this alone is not evidence of a structural change. [TWAIT001]
